memory_update.text: ALM is the clearest US-listed direct asset-owner exposure to non-Chinese tungsten supply; verify Sangdong ramp, processing pathway, and defense qualification/offtake details.
KMT is a stronger underfollowed mid-cap discovery candidate than defense primes because tungsten carbide, powders, penetrators, and armor are embedded inside an industrial tooling label.
TUNGF is a below-$300M speculative exception only; survival in later layers requires binding offtake, NI 43-101 support, financing, permitting, metallurgy, and credible production timing.

Global Tungsten & Powders is highly relevant to the node but private/Plansee-owned; use it as a customer/processor validation anchor for public upstream candidates rather than as an investable candidate.

Need a separate non-US/ADR pass for listed tungsten processors and miners in Canada, Australia, Europe, Vietnam/Korea-linked entities, and Japan; current pass was constrained to US-listed or US-tradable names.

ALM is the primary US-listed direct reference candidate for non-Chinese tungsten mine/oxide capacity; needs verification of Sangdong ramp, oxide/APT-equivalent processing, offtake, and defense-compliant origin.
KMT is the best underfollowed US-listed downstream processor/component candidate due to tungsten powders, carbide, penetrators, armor, aerospace and defense exposure.
GMTL is a small-cap NYSE American exploration/development candidate for US tungsten feedstock; its survival in later layers depends on PFS, metallurgy, permits, and processing/offtake path.
TUNGF is a micro-cap speculative shadow candidate tied to IMA Mine restart; include only with strict evidence gates because it is not yet a producer or processor.

Key Western APT/powder processors such as Global Tungsten & Powders and Buffalo Tungsten/Sandvik may be important chokepoint assets, but direct US-listed pure-play exposure is limited; later layers should map private processors and public parents.

The investable node may split into three tiers: immediate processor/component exposure (KMT, Sandvik context), near-term non-Chinese mine/oxide exposure (ALM), and future US concentrate feedstock developers (GMTL, TUNGF).

ALM is the clearest US-listed direct tungsten supply reference for the non-Chinese APT/defense-qualified tungsten node, but survival requires proof of Sangdong ramp, conversion route, offtakes, and defense qualification.

KMT is a likely underfollowed second-order candidate: an industrial tooling label may hide tungsten carbide, metallurgical powder, aerospace/defense and armor exposure, but raw-material cost and sourcing risk must be tested.

GMTL is a speculative shadow candidate for domestic tungsten mine supply because of Nevada assets and a DPA-funded Pilot Mountain PFS, but it is exploration-stage and not yet a processor or qualified supplier.

UAMY adds a hidden tungsten option through Fostung claims inside an antimony processor story; current link to APT/powder/defense-qualified tungsten remains weak and must be verified before later-layer inclusion.

Need a dedicated search for private/non-US processors such as Global Tungsten & Powders, Metal Tech, Plansee and specialty gas suppliers to map which US-listed companies have supplier/customer dependency on the true APT-to-powder bottleneck.

The node should be split in later layers into upstream mine/concentrate, APT/tungsten oxide conversion, tungsten powder/carbide, defense-qualified penetrator/armor/tooling, and semiconductor WF6 precursor chains.
ALM is the primary US-listed reference name for non-Chinese tungsten mine supply and planned tungsten oxide capacity; track but do not treat as underfollowed after CNBC/current-media attention.
KMT is the best underfollowed second-order candidate because it maps to tungsten carbide powders, defense tungsten solutions, penetrators, armor, and industrial tooling rather than to mining screens.

UAMY has tungsten optionality through Fostung, but current evidence shows exploration/resource-stage exposure with no Ontario commercial extraction or processing in 2025; keep as speculative shadow until development evidence improves.

TUNGF is a micro-cap speculative exception: possible direct US tungsten restart plus GTP LOI, but must be filtered hard for resource validity, financing, first production, binding offtake, and downstream qualification.

The US-listed universe lacks obvious pure-play APT processors because major US tungsten processors such as Global Tungsten & Powders and Elmet Technologies appear private; public exposure is mostly upstream miners/explorers or downstream carbide/tooling companies.

Layer 2 should separate three subnodes: mine/concentrate supply, APT/tungsten oxide/powder processing, and defense-qualified carbide/heavy-alloy components. The investable bottleneck may sit more in processing/qualification than ore ownership.

node: Tungsten APT processing and non-Chinese defense-qualified tungsten supply
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-tradable universe for the non-Chinese tungsten/APT/powder/carbide chokepoint. The direct public universe is thin: the clearest asset-owner is Almonty; the clearest US-listed downstream tungsten carbide/defense processor is Kennametal; Sandvik is a large-cap OTC ADR reference leader because it owns an integrated European tungsten chain; American Tungsten is a micro-cap OTC speculative shadow candidate tied to a potential Idaho restart and GTP offtake LOI. Global Tungsten & Powders appears highly relevant but is private/Plansee-owned, so it is used as evidence/context rather than a candidate. Expanded the US-listed universe for the tungsten APT / non-Chinese defense-qualified tungsten node. The strongest direct public-market exposure found is Almonty Industries, now Nasdaq-listed, with non-Chinese tungsten mine and oxide-processing ambitions. The most relevant underfollowed processor / downstream supplier is Kennametal, which has explicit tungsten carbide, tungsten powders, penetrators, armor, aerospace and defense exposure. Two small-cap discovery/speculative mine-developer candidates, Guardian Metal Resources and American Tungsten, provide possible future US tungsten concentrate feedstock but still require resource, permitting, processing, offtake, and defense-qualification verification. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the US-listed universe around the tungsten APT / non-Chinese defense-qualified supply node.
